chapter: Opinions, Edgar Battle and closing stories
title: Four-drummer records for Coral and closing remarks

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Just to cover one or two more odds and ends, there's in, I'm looking right now at an article that Dan Morgenstern did on you for Downbeat in the March 20, 1969 issue, it was a very nice article, and he mentioned that you had done another record with four drummers for Choral with Bobby Rosengarden, Specs Powell and Jimmy Crawford. That's before the one that you did with Krupa and Ray McKinley.

And Panama, that's right. We had all different rhythms on this other one that I did. Well one of them was that "Big Noise from Winnetka." See, and all I wanted Specs Powell to just play the tympany, Jimmy Crawford just to play that cymbal. Bobby Rosengarden to play the 6-8 time, and me I'd just weave in between all of them.
So was it all pretty successful?
Yes, yes, they all made a little noise there. The promotion wasn't that great on it.

And then the other ones there, when I had Gene Krupa and Ray McKinley and Panama as my guests, that made a little noise too, very commercial records. Each one of us had a track, and we played very good commercial tunes. Like 'My Blue Heaven' or something like that. (HUMMING) Gene would have that break (HUMMING) maybe Ray McKinley would have that break.
Let's see, 'I Love Paris', 'Dream', 'You're the Top', things like that.

Yeah, and so it would be like a dancer, stop time. This one has this, everybody had their charts and the earphones up there. And we had another drummer that just kept time. And we didn't have to keep time, all we had to do was fill in where we'd come in.
Yeah, was a good--Henry Jerome was his idea. But it just never took on; maybe if we did it now again with some kind of setup, maybe a little different thing going, maybe it'll catch on.
You never know about those things.
So much is depending on timing.
That's right. Timing and promotion. Who's doing it, where to put it. And who would ever thing 'Topsy' would have took off the way it did, because that was what? Rhythm and Blues with ....
